items.statement: At baseline, corresponding physical and emotional domains of the instruments had moderate-to-strong correlations. EORTC QLQ-C30 physical functioning correlated with the EQ-5D index at 0.70 and EQ VAS at 0.64, and emotional functioning correlated with EQ-5D anxiety/depression at -0.64.

items.statement: EQ-5D index and EQ VAS scores discriminated between tumor stages and ECOG performance groups. Scores were lower for more severe disease and poorer performance.

items.statement: Across all analyzed patients, the EQ-5D index increased by 0.04 and EQ VAS increased by 7.00 points after three months of treatment.
source: Full article, Results > Responsiveness, paragraph 1
Full article, Table 4 > Change in score

items.statement: Responsiveness differed by anchor-defined change group. EQ-5D index responsiveness was strongest in the improvement group and absent in the no-change group; EQ VAS responsiveness was large in the improvement group but weak in the worsened group.
source: Full article, Results > Responsiveness, paragraph 1
Full article, Table 4 > ES and SRM

items.statement: Distribution-based mean MCID estimates were 0.10 to 0.15 for the EQ-5D index and 4.01 to 7.56 for EQ VAS. Anchor-based average MCIDs were 0.04 and 4.00, respectively. The ROC-based index threshold was 0.20, but discrimination was limited.

items.statement: MCID-to-MDC ratios were below one at the individual level and above one at the group level. Thus, the estimated changes exceeded measurement error for groups but not for individuals.

items.statement: The authors concluded that the EQ-5D had good psychometric properties and could detect change and discriminate between levels of health among Ethiopian patients with cervical cancer.
source: Full article, Conclusion

items.statement: The authors concluded that the MCID estimates were clinically meaningful at the group level but did not support individual-level interpretation. They recommended further individual-level studies.
